relevance: The claimed proof (20 November 2026): a four-page note plus a Lean 4 archive (about 175,000 files) proving Mathlib's statement RiemannHypothesis and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions. Independent proof checkers accept it (A. Sutherland's verification page, https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/), but no readable proof exists. It is the primary source for all current work on this problem: checking the formal statements and definitions, reproducing the checks, and mapping the formal proof into readable mathematics (direction D-38). Not peer-reviewed; the Clay Institute still lists RH as open.
title: Note on a proof of the Riemann hypothesis found with Claude (with the Lean 4 archive)

authors: Afonso S. Bandeira, Dustin G. Mixon, Stefan Steinerberger
relevance: Proves c√n ≤ C_n ≤ n. The √n lower bound is probabilistic, via the dual ratio π₊(T)/ρ₁(T) for T = −(√n)/4 I + W with W a Rademacher Wigner matrix. Section 3 gives an iterative diagonal-pivot factorization that also costs at most n·tr(A), notes that it is typically much cheaper than the eigendecomposition, and asks whether that improvement can be made precise. Any direction aimed at the gap should start from this reduction and this factorization.
title: A lower bound for the Balan–Jiang matrix problem

authors: Jonathan W. Bober, Oleksiy Klurman et al.
relevance: Establishes Littlewood polynomials of arbitrarily large degree with normalised Mahler measure greater than 0.954, via mixed character sums. This is the current limsup record. A new direction should either beat this constant by a different construction or produce certified finite-degree polynomials that exceed the character-sum examples at the same length.
title: Distribution of mixed character sums and extremal problems for Littlewood polynomials
